newsitem.title: UK: British retail sales grow in May, but no boom.
newsitem.headline: British retail sales grow in May, but no boom.

text.p: British retail sales showed steady growth in May but there was no sign of a consumer spending boom, according to a leading business survey published on Tuesday.

The British Retail Consortium (BRC) said retail sales grew 4.8 percent year-on-year in May after an upward revised April growth rate of 4.1 percent. This compared with growth of 6.2 percent in the year to May 1996.
"Although May was a relatively good month for retailers, there is no sign of a runaway consumer boom," the BRC said.
In the three months to May, retail sales grew 4.2 percent in value from the same 1996 period.

The BRC said there was little evidence of any general boost from "windfall" bonuses for the members of mutually owned home loan societies and insurers who get free shares when the firms turn themselves into public companies. The exception, perhaps, is sales of larger electrical items.
Millions of Britons will receive shares worth a total of around 30 billion pounds as these companies are floated on the stock exchange.

"May appears to have been a good month for most retail sectors," said Andrew Higginson, chairman of the BRC economic affairs committee. "The month finished on a stronger note but thankfully we are a long way from runaway 'boom' conditions in the high street."

He said retailers accepted the need for recent modest interest rate increases but saw no case for tax rises in the July 2 budget. Base rates have risen in two stages to 6.5 percent from 6.0 percent at the beginning of May.
Andrew Sentance, chief economic adviser to the BRC, said a number of factors could slow spending growth in the months ahead.
"Recent rises in interest rates will push up mortgage rates and this is likely to hold back the housing market recovery which is supporting some retail sectors," he said.
"If there are tax rises in the Chancellor's forthcoming budget, this would reinforce any slowdown in the growth of spending later this year."
